text:
alex: Heads up — perf CI alarm after the 1.12 merge. 95p latency on the KV cache path jumped ~2.3x. Traces point at kernel selection changes. cc @jia @maria :rotating_light:

maria: saw the alert. do we have a CI link? can someone repro locally?

alex: CI run is here: https://ci.redwood.example/perf/1942109876 — ci-bot flagged regression on release candidate.

jia: I'll kick off a bisect now. my hunch is the kernel-selector heuristics commit from last week.

ops-bot: Perf bisect job queued: perf-bisect/1942109876 — starting.

jia: bisect narrowed it to commit a1b2c3f (kernel selector heuristics tweak). running targeted perf profile against that commit.

sam: can you paste the flamegraph or a short profile?

jia: flamegraph link: https://perf.redwood.example/flame/1942109876, short summary: extra memcpy in KV encode path + fallback to fused-attn for short batches (<=8).

alex: fused-attn for short batches? heuristics were supposed to avoid fused for short seqs to reduce overhead.

jia: found the diff — compare changed from >16 to >=16 in selector: that flips boundary when avg_seq == 16. small but explains the regression on our short-seq workloads. snippet:

```
// before
prefer_fused = avg_seq > 16
// after (accidental)
prefer_fused = avg_seq >= 16
```

maria: proposal: revert that commit on release-1.12 and cherry-pick the revert to 1.11 (stable). any objections? :thinking_face:

leo: agree with revert. also want a quick check on quantized path — fused kernels interact weirdly with int8 layouts.

alex: i'll open the revert PR against release-1.12 and run perf CI. will include a small unit test for the boundary.

ci-bot: Perf CI triggered: perf-ci/release-1.12-revert-a1b2c3f — waiting for results.

jia: ran perf CI on the revert branch locally and in CI — latency back to baseline on the KV path. attaching perf numbers in the PR.

maria: excellent. PR: https://git.redwood.example/r/revert-kernel-selector-a1b2c3f — includes perf graphs and the code comment fix. requesting 2 approvals.

sam: after merge we should backport to 1.11 and add an integration test that hits avg_seq==16 boundary repeatedly (regression guard).

alex: added test CL and pushed to release-1.11 branch (cherry-pick CL 7901). CI for 1.11 backport queued.

ops-bot: Deploy gate: release-1.12 revert requires 2 approvals and perf-ci green before rollout.

maria: tagging @eng-sre for rollout window and monitoring.

eng-sre: we can do a canary deploy at 03:00 UTC for 30m on dedicated pool. will watch 95p latency, KV hit ratio, and GC stalls.

alex: after merge I'll run a canary against the dedicated pool and keep an autoscale buffer to avoid capacity-driven noise.

jia: FYI also found a subtle kernel-registry ordering bug — the registry returned the fused kernel earlier than expected for equivalent cost. i'll open a follow-up PR with a comment + small fix.

maria: thanks all :thumbsup: once revert is landed and canary is green we'll merge backports and close the thread.

alex: reverting now, will post merge + perf CI green in a follow-up message.

ci-bot: Perf CI passed for revert branch — latency returned to baseline.

alex: revert merged to release-1.12, cherry-pick applied to release-1.11, 1.11 CI green. scheduling canary at 03:00 UTC.

maria: marking this as resolved from a release-blocker standpoint. follow-ups: add boundary unit test, registry ordering fix, and docs for kernel heuristics.

sam: i'll pick up the unit test and add it to the regression-suite.

eng-sre: will takeover monitoring during canary window. ping if traces spike.

alex: thanks team — great quick turnaround.
